overview: This heterogeneous State Department decimal-file bundle concerns Japanese-controlled or strategically sensitive aviation and transportation between 1940 and 1942. It begins with reports on military restrictions, equipment shortages, safety problems, and route expansion in Japanese civil aviation, including services to Palau, Saipan, Thailand, and a proposed Manila connection; it also includes a cross-reference about aviation-fuel shipments to Hainan. Later documents report naval and industrial activity around Maizuru and examine the controversial Japanese airline concession in Portuguese Timor, Australian and British security concerns, Portuguese neutrality, and the absence of local defenses. The final papers shift to Bolivia and the impracticability of using German insurance funds to acquire Junkers-owned shares in Lloyd Aéreo Boliviano, while administrative sheets and cross-references document how these materials were filed and circulated.

subfiles.title: Naval attaché report on restrictions on the Yokohama–Palau airline
subfiles.from: H. H. Smith-Hutton, Naval Attaché, Tokyo
subfiles.to: Office of Naval Intelligence and listed military recipients
subfiles.about: Reports that the new Yokohama–Saipan–Palau service was closed to civilians and foreigners under Japanese military regulations.
subfiles.summary: Report: Japan restricts most civil routes to military officers, citing aircraft shortages, while weighing a reciprocal US feeder service.

subfiles.title: Military attaché report on the Japan–Thailand air service
subfiles.to: G-2, War Department, and distribution recipients
subfiles.about: Describes the opening and strategic limitations of scheduled Japanese air service between Taiwan, China, and Thailand.
subfiles.summary: Report: a new 1940 Japan-Thailand air route detours around French Indochina, limiting payload and competitiveness with US mail service.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference on aviation-gasoline stocks at Hainan
subfiles.about: References a telegram concerning Japanese orders for large stocks of aviation gasoline destined for South China and Hainan.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: Japanese buyers ordered US aviation gasoline for delivery to South China and Hainan before October 1940.

subfiles.title: Charge-out card for files 894.796/56–59
subfiles.about: Records the administrative charging out of four numbered documents from the file.
subfiles.summary: Charge card records a 1949 file transfer, an administrative record with no substantive content.

subfiles.title: Hoover letter transmitting intelligence on Japanese air and naval matters
subfiles.about: Transmits an FBI memorandum based on information from a confidential source about Japanese naval and aviation activity.
subfiles.summary: Hoover forwards confidential intelligence on Japanese air and naval matters to State and military intelligence.

subfiles.title: FBI memorandum on Maizuru naval and industrial activity
subfiles.to: Adolf A. Berle Jr. and intelligence recipients
subfiles.about: Summarizes confidential observations of Japanese naval preparations, shipbuilding, aircraft-industry changes, and the Izumo Maru.
subfiles.summary: FBI memo reports Japanese warship construction and tight security at Maizuru, factory conversion to military production, and suspected sabotage aboard the Izumo Maru.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to the FBI memorandum on Maizuru
subfiles.about: Directs researchers to Hoover's letter and its enclosure concerning Japanese activity around Maizuru.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: Hoover's letter enclosed an FBI memo on Japanese military activity around Maizuru.

subfiles.title: Far Eastern Affairs digest of Portuguese press comment on the Timor airline
subfiles.about: Summarizes Portuguese press rebuttals to British concern over Japan's new airline to Portuguese Timor.
subfiles.summary: Memo digests Portuguese press debate over whether Japan's Timor airline threatens to turn the colony into another Indochina.

subfiles.title: Lisbon despatch no. 292 on British and Portuguese reactions to the Timor airline
subfiles.about: Reports Australian and British security concerns and a Portuguese press defense of the Japanese airline concession in Timor.
subfiles.summary: Lisbon reports Australian alarm and British press warnings over Japan's Timor airline, while Portugal insists it granted Japan the same terms as Britain.

subfiles.title: Lisbon despatch no. 295 quoting Diário de Lisboa
subfiles.about: Provides further Portuguese press defense of equal airline concessions to Japan and Australia.
subfiles.summary: Lisbon despatch: a Portuguese paper says both Timor airline concessions aim to boost the colony's economy, denying favoritism to Japan.

subfiles.title: Instruction to obtain the terms of Japanese engagements concerning Macau and Timor
subfiles.about: Orders the Lisbon legation to determine the exact terms of Japanese commitments to Portugal concerning Macau and Timor.
subfiles.summary: State asks for the exact terms of Japan's agreements with Portugal over Macau and Timor.

subfiles.title: Lisbon telegram no. 721 on the Japanese–Portuguese Timor agreement
subfiles.about: Reports Portuguese assurances that the Timor air-service agreement contained no secret provisions.
subfiles.summary: Lisbon denies secret clauses in the Japan-Timor airline deal, noting Portugal fears Dutch more than Japanese ambitions there.

subfiles.title: Internal memorandum on releasing frozen funds for a proposed visit
subfiles.from: Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Maxwell M. Hamilton
subfiles.to: Dean Acheson and the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Recommends Treasury clearance for the release of frozen funds connected with an otherwise unidentified proposed visit.
subfiles.summary: Memo on releasing frozen funds for an unspecified visit notes War and Navy raised no objection.

subfiles.title: La Paz despatch on purchasing Junkers-owned Lloyd Aéreo Boliviano stock
subfiles.from: Allan Dawson, First Secretary of Embassy, for the Ambassador
subfiles.about: Explains why German insurance debts could not practicably be used to purchase Junkers' shares in Lloyd Aéreo Boliviano.
subfiles.summary: Despatch finds a plan to buy Junkers' Bolivian airline shares impractical, especially after Bolivia broke relations with Germany.

subfiles.title: Department of State review sheet for the LAB stock despatch
subfiles.about: Records the review and processing of the La Paz despatch concerning Junkers-owned LAB stock.
subfiles.summary: Review sheet logs processing of a 1942 La Paz despatch on purchasing Junkers' Bolivian airline stock.

interest: Shows prewar Japanese military control of civil aviation, and a Timor airline dispute testing Portuguese neutrality.
